page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core architecture designed for memory-intensive workloads that require lower compute licensing overhead. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance exposes 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an extensive 260 MB shared L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX.

The primary resource focus of the server is its high memory-to-vCPU allocation, delivering 128.0 GB of RAM, or 32.0 GB per vCPU. The server lacks bundled local disk storage and includes zero local GPUs, relying instead on attached premium network storage volumes. Benchmark profiles show strong single-threaded capabilities, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2126.0 and 31.33 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. However, overall multi-core throughput remains constrained by the 4-vCPU cap, as reflected in lower multi-core stress-ng tests (3989.54) and uncached memory write bandwidth of 24.77 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is centered on optimizing per-core licensing expenses. By configuring high RAM density across fewer vCPUs, operations such as enterprise relational databases or large in-memory caches avoid the software licensing penalties associated with full-socket provisioning. The instance is suited for enterprise relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, and memory-bound ETL batch jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor within the Hyper-V environment. Featuring a constrained vCPU configuration, it allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores) paired with 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an expansive 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The architecture includes 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage is absent, requiring attached remote storage. The server yields strong single-core benchmarks, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2126.0 and high single-threaded compression performance. Due to core count limits, multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth benchmark in the lower percentiles. The hardware profile is engineered to maximize memory density while reducing per-core commercial software licensing costs, making it well matched for in-memory caching, enterprise database deployments, and large-footprint analytics processing.
